Title: Research Informatics Data Engineer
Place: Copenhagen, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
Description:
Build the digital foundation for scientific discovery

Every day, researchers rely on digital technologies to design experiments, generate data, and make scientific decisions.

We are looking for a Research Informatics Engineer who enjoys combining scientific understanding with technical expertise to build practical digital solutions that help researchers make better use of their data.

This is an engineering-focused Research Informatics role where you will help implement, configure and connect commercial scientific platforms, and build the data flows and integrations that enable modern research.

Your new role

At Lundbeck, Research Informatics works at the intersection of science, data and technology. We collaborate closely with researchers, colleagues across Lundbeck Global IT, and technology partners to implement, integrate and continuously improve the scientific systems, research data and digital workflows that support modern drug discovery.

As research becomes increasingly digital and data-driven, our role is to ensure that scientific systems evolve with the science, research data becomes a trusted asset, and digital technologies create real value for researchers.

You will join the Research Informatics team within Global Research. Working closely with researchers, colleagues across Lundbeck Global IT and technology vendors, you will help implement, configure and improve the digital platforms used across Research. You will contribute to scientific applications, research data and digital workflows that enable researchers to work more efficiently and make better use of their data.

This is a hands-on role where you will combine scientific understanding with technical skills to deliver practical digital solutions that support discovery research.

What you will do:

Support scientific applications


Work with researchers to gather, analyse and document business and scientific requirements for new digital capabilities.
Implement, configure and maintain scientific applications supporting Global Research.
Work with researchers to understand scientific workflows and translate research needs into practical digital solutions.
Support application lifecycle management, testing, documentation and user support.
Collaborate with colleagues across Lundbeck Global IT (EDE) and technology vendors to continuously improve the scientific application landscape.



Connect research data


Contribute to connecting research data across the digital research landscape.
Implement and support data flows, metadata models and integrations between scientific applications.
Apply FAIR data principles to improve the quality, accessibility and reuse of research data.
Help establish trusted research data that supports today's science and tomorrow's advanced analytics and AI.



Improve digital research


Identify opportunities to improve scientific workflows through better digital solutions.
Participate in implementation of new technologies and enhancements to existing platforms.
Contribute to testing, training and knowledge sharing.
Collaborate across Research, Lundbeck Global IT (EDE) and external partners to continuously improve the digital research environment.



Your future team

Research Informatics is a collaborative team with expertise spanning life sciences, laboratory informatics, research data management and digital technologies.

Together we build and continuously improve the scientific systems, research data and digital workflows that underpin discovery research. We combine scientific understanding with technical expertise to ensure our digital capabilities evolve alongside the science they support.

The position is based at Lundbeck Headquarters in Valby.

What You Bring To The Team

You are curious about science and motivated by solving practical problems through technology. You enjoy understanding how research is performed and using that understanding to build better systems, better research data and better digital workflows.

You are motivated by building and improving digital solutions that scientists rely on, and enjoy turning scientific needs into robust systems, integrations and data flows.

Required Qualifications


MSc in Life Sciences, Computer Science, Engineering or another relevant scientific or technical discipline.
Strong understanding of scientific research workflows.
Experience from pharmaceutical, biotechnology or academic research.



You Have Experience With Several Of The Following

You have experience working with scientific systems, research data and digital workflows and enjoy translating scientific needs into practical technical solutions. Experience with requirements gathering and using modern AI-assisted development tools to improve productivity, including large language models (LLMs) for coding and technical problem solving, is an advantage.


Business and scientific requirements gathering
Using large language models (LLMs) and AI-assisted development tools to support coding, scripting and technical problem solving
FAIR data principles and research data management
Data flows between scientific applications
Metadata and scientific data models
Scientific applications and laboratory informatics
Configuration of commercial scientific software
Systems integration and APIs
Python or other scripting languages
SQL, relational databases and modern data platforms
Cloud-based scientific platforms



Experience with in vivo research and biologics, including antibody discovery, is an advantage.

Personal qualities


Enjoys solving problems in collaboration with others.
Is curious and eager to learn.
Takes a structured approach to your work.
Communicates effectively with both scientific and technical colleagues.
Enjoys working across scientific and technical disciplines.



Our promise to you

Lundbeck offers an inspiring workplace and innovative culture, where our curiosity, accountability and adaptability enable us to transform lives. We want to go faster and further on addressing the big unmet needs of people living with brain disorders. We offer rewarding careers with a mix of exciting tasks and development opportunities that are balanced with initiatives focused on your well-being.

We need every brain in the game, and at Lundbeck, we are committed to building a workforce that is as diverse as the people we serve. Read more about our commitment at www.lundbeck.com/global/about-us/our-commitment/diversity-and-inclusion.

Annual base salary range: (582 000 - 799 700) DKK gross

At Lundbeck, we are committed to fair and transparent pay. Please note that the final base salary within the stated range will be based on relevant qualifications, skills, competencies, and level of proficiency as well as internal pay equity.

Title: Data Engineer
Description:
Hos Knowit skaber vi digitale kundeoplevelser og løsninger for nogle af landets mest ambitiøse virksomheder. Data og AI spiller en stadig større rolle i den udvikling, og vi arbejder tæt sammen med både Google og Microsoft. Derfor leder vi nu efter en Data Engineer, der kan tage teknisk ejerskab for big data-delen på et af vores største kundeprogrammer.

Din rolle som Data Engineer

Du bliver en del af et fast, tværfagligt team i Aarhus, hvor udviklere, specialister og rådgivere arbejder sammen om den samme løsning. Her er du med til at bygge og drifte det dataøkosystem, som både forretning, redaktører og digitale services læner sig op ad hos en af vores store globale kunder.

I dit daglige opgave vil du have bidrage til og ofte have ansvaret for:


At eje og udvide rygraden i vores dataflow, bygget med data fra webanalyse, søgeperformance, indholdssystemer og andre eksterne signaler ind i data warehouse.
Bygge og vedligeholde afledte dataprodukter, for eksempel content scoring og user segmentation, som andre services og redaktører bruger til rangering og prioritering
Føde downstream marketing- og CRM-platforme ved at batche brugeraktivitet og samtykkedata ind i Salesforce Data Cloud, Salesforce Marketing Cloud og en marketing automation-platform
Modellere data til både analytisk og operationel brug, med et vedvarende blik for datakvalitet og sporbarhed
Tage ejerskab for det, vi sender i produktion, og holde øje med det, når det kører



Hvem er du?

Vi forestiller os, at du kan genkende dig selv i flere af punkterne nedenfor, også selvom ikke alle passer på din profil.


Har stor erfaring med SQL, og solid praktisk erfaring med BigQuery på Google Cloud, herunder datasæt, views, routines og query-performance.
Har et solidt data engineering-fundament på Google Cloud, altså erfaring med at bygge og drifte pipelines i produktion.
Er en øvet softwareudvikler, for eksempel i Python, så du kan bevæge dig mellem værktøjer i stedet for at være låst til én teknologi.
Bruger AI-kodeassistenter og agentiske arbejdsgange som en naturlig del af din hverdag, og tager nye AI-værktøjer i brug, efterhånden som de kommer.
Kan rådgive kunder om dataarkitektur og big data-opsætninger
Du har arbejdet med customer data platforms og CRM-dataflows, for eksempel Salesforce Data Cloud og Marketing Cloud, samt samtykkebevidst datahåndtering

Title: Analyst, Portfolio Management

Description:
Drive Meaningful Change

Are you ready to drive meaningful change in the Danish pharmacy market? As an Analyst, Portfolio Management in our BD DK team, you’ll work closely with the Specialist, Portfolio Management to develop and maintain our DK Pharmacy portfolio. You’ll combine supportive responsibilities with ownership of initiatives that drive growth and improve performance, focusing on pricing, portfolio analysis, market-tool development, and automation of workflows.

At Abacus Medicine, you’ll join our BD DK team consisting of dedicated professionals and student analysts working together to make a real difference in the Danish pharmacy- and hospital market. We’re ambitious and aim to set the standard for excellence in our field.

We value a supportive environment, personal development, and teamwork. Here, you’ll have the chance to take responsibility, challenge how things are done, and grow as part of a caring and driven team.

Realize Your Opportunities as a Portfolio Analyst

Supporting and developing the DK Pharmacy portfolio
Setting prices in collaboration with the Pricing team, ensuring accuracy and compliance.
Analyzing portfolio performance and sharing insights with internal and external stakeholders.
Helping to develop and improve tools for market analysis.
Automating portfolio workflows using coding and data collection.
Supporting product launches and lifecycle decisions with evidence-based analysis.
Preparing performance reports, forecasts, and ad-hoc analyses.
Monitoring market and regulatory developments, escalating risks, and proposing solutions.


Fuel for your success in the role

The ideal candidate is driven to get better every day and motivated by the ambition to help our team become the leader in the Danish pharmacy market. You’re curious, structured, and eager to learn—always looking for ways to sharpen your skills and contribute your share to our common goal.

You have a genuine interest in technical solutions and automation. Here, you’ll have the freedom and responsibility to use or develop your coding skills to automate tasks and support data-driven decisions that give us a competitive edge.

You thrive in a busy environment, enjoy working with a variety of tasks, and know that your actions make a real difference for the team and the business.

Furthermore, We Hope That These Factors Describe You


You hold a Master's Degree in business, economics or a related field.
Proficiency in data analysis tool and Microsoft Excel.
Fluency in English and Danish or another Scandinavian language.


Can you see yourself becoming our new Analyst, Portfolio Management?

Title: Product Manager, Data Insights
Description:
About Us

nShift is the leading global provider of cloud delivery management solutions (SaaS), we enable the frictionless shipment and return of almost one billion shipments across 190 countries each year. We are headquartered in London and Oslo and have over 500 employees across offices in Sweden, Finland, Norway, Denmark, the United Kingdom, Poland, the Netherlands, Belgium, and Romania.

Our software is used by many of the world leading e-commerce, retail, manufacturing, and 3PL shippers due to us having over 1000 carriers integrated into our platform, nearly 3 times more than our competitors!

If you buy goods online, there is a strong chance that nShift has powered that delivery, so come and join us as we shape the future of shipping, one frictionless journey at a time.

About You

You think like a product manager and work like a data scientist. You have shipped ML-powered products to real customers and can point to the decisions you made, not just the ones made around you. Messy data, ambiguous model outputs, and stakeholders who don't yet see why the data matters are familiar territory.

You think in terms of compounding: how every data point collected today improves predictions tomorrow, and how that improvement builds a position competitors cannot close. Data insights is nShift's path from a tool company to an intelligence platform, and that scope motivates you rather than overwhelming you.

You are as comfortable in a Jupyter notebook as in a leadership meeting, and you know when each is needed.

Purpose of role

The mission is to define what nShift builds with that data, validate it before engineering commits, and ship intelligence products that help shippers make better decisions. A shipper asking "how can I improve my delivery experience" should get an answer powered by the full network, not just their own history. Done well, that becomes a compounding intelligence layer: every data point collected today improves suggestions tomorrow, and the improvement creates a position no competitor can close.

The intelligence layer draws from two sources. Structured operational data, such as shipment telemetry and carrier performance, feeds statistical models and predictions. Qualitative data, such as customer support interactions, delivery exception messages, and community feedback, carries signal that numbers alone cannot surface. LLMs make that signal extractable and usable at scale. This role owns both.

The role sits at the intersection of product management and data science. You have the technical depth to build ML proof-of-concepts independently and the commercial judgment to translate those capabilities into products customers pay for. You write the strategy and the first notebook.

What You'll Be Doing

Define and own the data driven product strategy


Own the roadmap for nShift's data intelligence layer: carrier performance prediction, cross-customer benchmarking, ML-driven carrier recommendations, and related capabilities.
Translate nShift's data asset into a sequenced product strategy that delivers near-term value while building toward the compounding intelligence layer vision.
Define the information architecture for the data insights layer: what data is collected, how it is normalized (in partnership with adjacent teams), and how it is exposed to upstream products.
Make hard prioritization calls: what to build first to validate the ML hypothesis, what to defer, and what to kill when the data doesn't support the bet.
Own the qualitative intelligence pipeline alongside the quantitative one: define which unstructured sources carry decision-relevant signal (support tickets, delivery exception messages, customer forum, carrier communications), how LLM-extracted insights are structured for downstream use, and how qualitative and quantitative signals combine into a coherent intelligence product.
Own the positioning and differentiation narrative: why this dataset is uniquely nShift's, why no competitor can replicate it, and how to articulate that defensibility to enterprise buyers.



Build and validate before engineering commits


Run ML proof-of-concepts independently: data exploration, feature engineering, model selection, and initial validation, using Python, notebooks, and the data available in nShift's data layer.
Define the evaluation framework for both ML models and LLM pipelines. For ML features: what accuracy thresholds matter, how to measure model performance in production, how to distinguish signal from noise. For LLM-based features: how to assess output consistency, factual grounding, and quality at scale, where traditional accuracy metrics don't apply.
Design lightweight experiments that answer the key questions before a full engineering team is committed. Does the prediction accuracy justify the product? Does cross-customer data improve the model significantly? Is the data we have sufficient, or do we need to instrument more?
Translate POC findings into clear build, kill, or iterate decisions backed by data.



Partner across data, engineering, and commercial teams


Work closely with engineers to define the data models, pipelines, and normalization standards needed to power ML features. You are a customer and co-designer of the data layer, not a passenger.
Drive integration of data insights capabilities into existing products. Work closly with your PM peers to make this happen.
Engage directly with customers and prospects across the full spectrum, from small shippers to global enterprises, to validate intelligence use cases: what decisions do they make today that better data would improve? What would they pay for? What do they trust?
Build the commercial narrative: ROI frameworks, value quantification, and positioning for the target buyer.



Govern the data responsibly


Define the anonymization, aggregation, and consent frameworks that make cross-customer benchmarking legally and ethically sound, and credible to enterprise customers who will ask hard questions.
Work with Legal and the DPO to ensure data usage within the intelligence layer meets GDPR and contractual obligations. The data asset is only valuable if customers trust nShift to use it appropriately.
Establish transparency standards for ML-powered recommendations: when does a merchant see why a carrier was recommended? What level of explainability builds trust without revealing proprietary network data?



What You'll Bring

Must-have


Hands-on data proficiency across both paradigms: you can build and validate ML proof-of-concepts (data exploration, feature engineering, model training, evaluation) using Python and standard ML tooling (scikit-learn, pandas, XGBoost, or equivalent), and you can design and evaluate LLM-based analysis pipelines (prompt design, retrieval-augmented approaches, output quality evaluation). You are not a data scientist or an ML engineer, but you can work like one when the problem requires it.
Shipped ML-powered products: you have personally driven an ML or data intelligence product from initial hypothesis to production, including defining evaluation criteria, partnering with data engineers and scientists, and making commercial decisions based on model performance data.
PM fundamentals with commercial depth: 3+ years shipping B2B SaaS products. You can build a business case, define pricing, run customer discovery, and hold direct conversations with enterprise buyers about ROI.
Data literacy that earns engineering respect: you understand data models, pipeline design, normalization challenges, and the practical constraints of real production data. You can review a data schema and immediately ask the right questions.
Clear communication across the technical and commercial boundary: you can explain a precision-recall tradeoff to a CPO and a carrier event data use case to a data engineer in the same afternoon, without condescending to either.
Excellent written and verbal English: you will write strategy documents, ML experiment briefs, customer-facing product narratives, and present to leadership, often in the same week.



Nice to have


Experience with time-series or logistics domain data: carrier performance modelling, routing optimization, ETA prediction, or related domains.
Familiarity with data platform concepts: data lake houses, feature stores, model registries, observability for ML in production.
Background in cross-customer benchmarking or network intelligence products, where the value comes from aggregation rather than individual customer data.
Experience with GDPR-compliant data product design in a multi-tenant B2B SaaS context.
Nordic or European logistics market experience: carrier landscape, regulatory environment, freight economics.
Track record of building the first data product at a company, defining standards rather than inheriting them.

Title: Product Manager, Data Insights
Description:
About Us

nShift is the leading global provider of cloud delivery management solutions (SaaS), we enable the frictionless shipment and return of almost one billion shipments across 190 countries each year. We are headquartered in London and Oslo and have over 500 employees across offices in Sweden, Finland, Norway, Denmark, the United Kingdom, Poland, the Netherlands, Belgium, and Romania.

Our software is used by many of the world leading e-commerce, retail, manufacturing, and 3PL shippers due to us having over 1000 carriers integrated into our platform, nearly 3 times more than our competitors!

If you buy goods online, there is a strong chance that nShift has powered that delivery, so come and join us as we shape the future of shipping, one frictionless journey at a time.

About You

You think like a product manager and work like a data scientist. You have shipped ML-powered products to real customers and can point to the decisions you made, not just the ones made around you. Messy data, ambiguous model outputs, and stakeholders who don't yet see why the data matters are familiar territory.

You think in terms of compounding: how every data point collected today improves predictions tomorrow, and how that improvement builds a position competitors cannot close. Data insights is nShift's path from a tool company to an intelligence platform, and that scope motivates you rather than overwhelming you.

You are as comfortable in a Jupyter notebook as in a leadership meeting, and you know when each is needed.

Purpose of role

The mission is to define what nShift builds with that data, validate it before engineering commits, and ship intelligence products that help shippers make better decisions. A shipper asking "how can I improve my delivery experience" should get an answer powered by the full network, not just their own history. Done well, that becomes a compounding intelligence layer: every data point collected today improves suggestions tomorrow, and the improvement creates a position no competitor can close.

The intelligence layer draws from two sources. Structured operational data, such as shipment telemetry and carrier performance, feeds statistical models and predictions. Qualitative data, such as customer support interactions, delivery exception messages, and community feedback, carries signal that numbers alone cannot surface. LLMs make that signal extractable and usable at scale. This role owns both.

The role sits at the intersection of product management and data science. You have the technical depth to build ML proof-of-concepts independently and the commercial judgment to translate those capabilities into products customers pay for. You write the strategy and the first notebook.

What You'll Be Doing

Define and own the data driven product strategy


Own the roadmap for nShift's data intelligence layer: carrier performance prediction, cross-customer benchmarking, ML-driven carrier recommendations, and related capabilities.
Translate nShift's data asset into a sequenced product strategy that delivers near-term value while building toward the compounding intelligence layer vision.
Define the information architecture for the data insights layer: what data is collected, how it is normalized (in partnership with adjacent teams), and how it is exposed to upstream products.
Make hard prioritization calls: what to build first to validate the ML hypothesis, what to defer, and what to kill when the data doesn't support the bet.
Own the qualitative intelligence pipeline alongside the quantitative one: define which unstructured sources carry decision-relevant signal (support tickets, delivery exception messages, customer forum, carrier communications), how LLM-extracted insights are structured for downstream use, and how qualitative and quantitative signals combine into a coherent intelligence product.
Own the positioning and differentiation narrative: why this dataset is uniquely nShift's, why no competitor can replicate it, and how to articulate that defensibility to enterprise buyers.



Build and validate before engineering commits


Run ML proof-of-concepts independently: data exploration, feature engineering, model selection, and initial validation, using Python, notebooks, and the data available in nShift's data layer.
Define the evaluation framework for both ML models and LLM pipelines. For ML features: what accuracy thresholds matter, how to measure model performance in production, how to distinguish signal from noise. For LLM-based features: how to assess output consistency, factual grounding, and quality at scale, where traditional accuracy metrics don't apply.
Design lightweight experiments that answer the key questions before a full engineering team is committed. Does the prediction accuracy justify the product? Does cross-customer data improve the model significantly? Is the data we have sufficient, or do we need to instrument more?
Translate POC findings into clear build, kill, or iterate decisions backed by data.



Partner across data, engineering, and commercial teams


Work closely with engineers to define the data models, pipelines, and normalization standards needed to power ML features. You are a customer and co-designer of the data layer, not a passenger.
Drive integration of data insights capabilities into existing products. Work closly with your PM peers to make this happen.
Engage directly with customers and prospects across the full spectrum, from small shippers to global enterprises, to validate intelligence use cases: what decisions do they make today that better data would improve? What would they pay for? What do they trust?
Build the commercial narrative: ROI frameworks, value quantification, and positioning for the target buyer.



Govern the data responsibly


Define the anonymization, aggregation, and consent frameworks that make cross-customer benchmarking legally and ethically sound, and credible to enterprise customers who will ask hard questions.
Work with Legal and the DPO to ensure data usage within the intelligence layer meets GDPR and contractual obligations. The data asset is only valuable if customers trust nShift to use it appropriately.
Establish transparency standards for ML-powered recommendations: when does a merchant see why a carrier was recommended? What level of explainability builds trust without revealing proprietary network data?



What You'll Bring

Must-have


Hands-on data proficiency across both paradigms: you can build and validate ML proof-of-concepts (data exploration, feature engineering, model training, evaluation) using Python and standard ML tooling (scikit-learn, pandas, XGBoost, or equivalent), and you can design and evaluate LLM-based analysis pipelines (prompt design, retrieval-augmented approaches, output quality evaluation). You are not a data scientist or an ML engineer, but you can work like one when the problem requires it.
Shipped ML-powered products: you have personally driven an ML or data intelligence product from initial hypothesis to production, including defining evaluation criteria, partnering with data engineers and scientists, and making commercial decisions based on model performance data.
PM fundamentals with commercial depth: 3+ years shipping B2B SaaS products. You can build a business case, define pricing, run customer discovery, and hold direct conversations with enterprise buyers about ROI.
Data literacy that earns engineering respect: you understand data models, pipeline design, normalization challenges, and the practical constraints of real production data. You can review a data schema and immediately ask the right questions.
Clear communication across the technical and commercial boundary: you can explain a precision-recall tradeoff to a CPO and a carrier event data use case to a data engineer in the same afternoon, without condescending to either.
Excellent written and verbal English: you will write strategy documents, ML experiment briefs, customer-facing product narratives, and present to leadership, often in the same week.



Nice to have


Experience with time-series or logistics domain data: carrier performance modelling, routing optimization, ETA prediction, or related domains.
Familiarity with data platform concepts: data lake houses, feature stores, model registries, observability for ML in production.
Background in cross-customer benchmarking or network intelligence products, where the value comes from aggregation rather than individual customer data.
Experience with GDPR-compliant data product design in a multi-tenant B2B SaaS context.
Nordic or European logistics market experience: carrier landscape, regulatory environment, freight economics.
Track record of building the first data product at a company, defining standards rather than inheriting them.

Title: Supply Chain Process Optimisation & Digitalisation Expert - ECCO HQ, Bredebro
Place: Bredebro, Region of Southern Denmark, Denmark
Description:
Would you like to shape the future of ECCO’s global supply chain by turning complex processes and data into smarter digital solutions?

Join ECCO’s Global Value Chain department and play a key role in strengthening how we work with process optimisation, analytics and digitalisation across our end-to-end supply chain. Here, you will help create the foundation for better decisions, more efficient processes and a stronger data-driven culture across the business.

Transform supply chain processes through data and digitalization

Based at ECCO HQ in Bredebro, you will join our Quantified Supply Chain team within Global Value Chain. Working closely with colleagues across Supply Planning, Market Fulfilment, S&OP, Forwarding and Distribution Network, you will help drive continuous improvements across our global operations.

In ECCO, we manage our supply chain from end to end. As we continue our digitalisation journey, we are looking for someone who can connect business processes, data and technology, transforming opportunities into practical solutions that create value. You will collaborate with stakeholders across the organisation, including IT, Data & AI, SAP teams and business leaders, helping ensure that data and digital tools become an integral part of how we work and make decisions.

Specifically, You Will


Develop and implement process optimisation and digitalisation solutions independently and in collaboration with business, IT and Data & AI teams.
Build and maintain automated data flows, reporting solutions and dashboards that improve transparency and support decision-making.
Drive advanced analytics, KPI frameworks and deep-dive business analyses to uncover opportunities and support strategic priorities.
Act as a trusted advisor on Power BI, Python and digital solutions, helping strengthen data literacy across Global Value Chain.
Lead communication, training and stakeholder engagement activities to support successful adoption of new processes and tools.


Create insights that support better business decisions

This role combines technical expertise with business understanding. Success comes from your ability to understand supply chain processes, identify optimisation opportunities and communicate insights in a way that inspires action.

You enjoy digging into data, challenging existing ways of working and turning complexity into clarity. At the same time, you know that lasting improvements are created through collaboration and strong stakeholder relationships.

To Thrive In This Role, We Imagine That You


Have experience with process optimisation, automation and digital transformation in a complex business environment.
Bring strong analytical and reporting capabilities, including hands-on experience with Power BI and data storytelling.
Have working knowledge of SQL and Python and feel comfortable working with large datasets and modern data platforms.
Understand supply chain processes, planning or inventory-related disciplines, or are motivated to deepen your expertise within these areas.
Communicate confidently in English and can engage stakeholders with different levels of technical understanding.


Help shape the next chapter of our digital supply chain journey

You will join a collaborative team where curiosity, knowledge sharing and continuous improvement are part of everyday life. We value new ideas and encourage initiative, giving you the opportunity to influence how we work with analytics, automation and digitalisation across the organisation.

This is a role with broad exposure across ECCO’s global value chain, allowing you to build a strong network while developing both your technical and business capabilities. If you are excited by the prospect of making a visible impact and helping shape the future of supply chain decision-making, we would love to hear from you.

We know that great candidates do not always meet every requirement. If this role excites you and you believe you can contribute, we encourage you to apply.

Ready to make your mark?

We review applications on an ongoing basis and the position is open until filled, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

For questions about the role, feel free to reach out to Manager, Quantified Supply Chain, Liudmyla Kovalchuk, on likov@ecco.com.

CREATE THE FOOTPRINTS OF TOMORROW

Join us and you become part of a meaningful, developing and multicultural workplace with colleagues who are proud to create the footprints of tomorrow. Our offices and facilities around the world have an informal culture and relaxed dress code – our shoe code is slightly stricter.

Are you curious, passionate and ready to make an impact? Then you’ll fit right in.

Design, build, and maintain production-grade GenAI applications and pipelines using Python, MLflow, Databricks, and leading AI platforms such as OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google.

You have experience using LLMs from multiple state-of-the-art providers of frontier and open-source models, and you have a deep understanding of the strengths and trade-offs of different frontier and open-source models.
You have experience building applications that leverage retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), tool calling, agents, or other modern LLM architectures.
You are comfortable developing solutions in Python and working with libraries such as Transformers and the SDKs of leading LLM Providers.
You are comfortable working in Databricks or similar cloud-based data and AI platforms, including building pipelines, workflows, model serving endpoints, and production deployments.
You have strong PySpark, Pandas, and SQL skills and are comfortable working with large, structured datasets.
You are comfortable taking ownership of projects, working independently, and collaborating directly with stakeholders across the business.

Impact: Ship AI and data solutions that create real impact in one of Europe’s fastest-growing companies.

Title: Data Analyst II
Description:
About ENSEK

ENSEK builds the cloud‑native SaaS software that’s transforming how energy retailers operate, innovate and manage at scale.

We help retailers lower operating costs, improve billing accuracy for consumers, and enhance customer experience through automation and AI‑driven insight, all underpinned by modern, cloud‑native architecture.

ENSEK is at an exciting inflection point as we scale at pace towards new international horizons. If you’re driven by solving complex, real‑world problems and want to build modern technology that accelerates the global energy transition, you’ll feel right at home with us.

About The Role

We are seeking a capable and proactive Data Analyst to join our Data Function. You will work closely with cross functional teams to translate business questions into clear analytical problems, deliver reliable insights, and support data‑driven decision‑making across the organisation.

You will independently build analyses, dashboards, and datasets that help teams understand performance, identify opportunities, and make informed decisions. You will be comfortable working with SQL, analytical tools, and visualisation platforms, and you will take responsibility for ensuring your outputs are accurate, well structured, and aligned to stakeholder needs.

This role is ideal for someone who has strong analytical foundations and is ready to take ownership of end-to-end analytical delivery.

Key responsibilities:


Translate business questions into clear analytical problems with defined scope and expected outcomes.
Independently query data using SQL and analytical tools to produce clean, reliable datasets for analysis.
Build and maintain dashboards and reports that support decision making across teams.
Validate outputs through checks, comparisons, and clear documentation to ensure accuracy and trust.
Communicate insights in practical, accessible terms to both technical and nontechnical audiences.
Work closely with stakeholders to understand their objectives and ensure analyses meet their needs.
Apply appropriate statistical techniques for common analytical problems and explain uncertainty clearly.
Ensure dashboards and reports remain up to date, accurate, and aligned with current metric definitions.
Follow data governance, security, and compliance standards when handling sensitive information.
Contribute to improving analytical processes, documentation, and team knowledge sharing.


Experience required:


Experience in a data analytics role with proven ability to deliver insights and reporting.
Proficiency in SQL for retrieving, joining, and manipulating data.
Experience building dashboards (preferably in Sigma) that support decision making.
Strong analytical thinking and problem framing skills.
Ability to communicate findings clearly to technical and nontechnical audiences.
Understanding of basic statistical concepts and how to apply them responsibly.
Strong attention to detail and commitment to producing accurate, reliable outputs.


Company Benefits


25 days’ holiday + bank holidays
Option to buy or sell 5 extra annual leave days per year
Vitality Health Insurance, including private healthcare, virtual GP access, mental‑health support and wellbeing perks (50% off gym memberships -Virgin Active, Nuffield, PureGym)
Pension with 5% matched contribution
Regular team‑wide and company‑wide events
2 volunteering days per year to give back
Remote‑first working environment with offices in London and Nottingham

Title: Senior Data Analyst
Description:
The Role:




Brook Green Supply (BGS) is a leading independent B2B gas and electricity supplier, delivering tailored energy supply and Net-Zero solutions to industrial and commercial consumers.




As a Senior Data Analyst, you will use advanced SQL and analytical skills to extract, transform and interpret data from large relational databases. You will design intuitive dashboards that turn complex data into clear, actionable insight, helping the business understand performance, identify trends, spot risks and opportunities, and make informed decisions.




You will ensure data accuracy and integrity by developing efficient SQL scripts for analysis, reporting and troubleshooting. Working closely with Data Engineers and the wider Tech team, you will streamline data processes, contribute to data models and provide insight that supports business decision-making.




This role suits an ambitious, flexible and technically strong analyst who enjoys explaining the story behind the data, improving reporting quality and helping colleagues use data with confidence.




Essential Functions of the Job:




Collaborate with cross-functional teams to gather data requirements and understand business needs.
Write, optimise and maintain complex SQL queries for data extraction, transformation and analysis across large datasets.
Clean, analyse and transform large and complex datasets into accurate, actionable information.
Identify trends, patterns and correlations in data to uncover insights that support business decision-making.
Perform ad hoc data analysis and provide clear recommendations based on findings.
Produce visually clear, engaging and user-friendly dashboards.
Validate data accuracy and quality to support reliable reporting.
Stay up to date with industry trends and best practice in data visualisation and analytics.
Present findings and insights to stakeholders in a clear and concise way.
Coach and mentor colleagues and new starters on data topics, helping the business unlock greater value from data.
Support improvements to data processes, reporting models and analytical ways of working.







Skills & Experience Required:




Proven experience as a Data Analyst or similar role, with a focus on data visualisation using Tableau.
Strong knowledge of SQL, with Python, R or similar programming languages desirable.
Demonstrated ability to write and optimise complex SQL queries for data extraction, transformation and analysis.
Experience working with large, structured datasets and producing accurate reporting outputs.
Strong technical background, with excellent analytical skills and high attention to detail.
Excellent verbal, written and presentation skills, with the ability to explain complex information to non-technical stakeholders.
Good knowledge of Microsoft Office and confidence working across multiple web-based platforms.
Experience using a CRM system is desirable.
Degree-level education in a numerical subject, with a STEM degree desirable.
Self-starter who takes ownership, creates solutions and improves business processes.
Able to work independently and as part of a team, prioritising workload effectively with minimal supervision.
Able to coach and mentor colleagues across the business on data topics.
Comfortable working in a fast-paced, evolving environment and responding to changing business needs.
Experience in the electricity or gas industry is not required, but is preferred.
Interest in developing knowledge across commercial decision-making, wholesale markets, non-commodities, forecasting, analytics and energy regulation.

Title: Senior Python Data Analyst
Description:
About Rare.

We empower our clients to navigate and capitalise on commercial opportunities within the healthcare market. Our expertise spans pharmaceutical and medical device manufacturers, healthc6are providers, and investors, helping them make informed, strategic decisions with confidence.




We provide up-to-date, accurate data through our proprietary Rare. SaaS products, enabling our customers to target previously invisible prospects, grow market share, and launch new products. We also deliver high-value bespoke market intelligence that brings clarity to the market. Our analysis lets providers monitor industry trends, assess market demand, and make data-driven decisions that improve their positioning and patient engagement.




Working for Rare.

We're a small consultancy and SaaS startup of around fifteen people, all working remotely with monthly/quarterly meetups where possible. We're primarily distributed across the UK, Ireland, Spain, and a growing delivery team in Paraguay. Our culture has a flat structure where everyone is a hands-on contributor to our success. We're looking for grounded professionals who thrive on ownership, are comfortable creating clarity out of ambiguity, and enjoy finding creative solutions to complex problems.




If you have a background in freelancing or contracting, you'll feel at home. We want to meet people with strong interpersonal skills who can take the lead and advocate for their ideas while taking priorities and feedback into account. Given the dual nature of our business, you should be comfortable working closely with both our consulting and SaaS product delivery teams, and with external clients and internal software engineers alike.




We believe work should be measured by outcomes and impact, not just outputs. In exchange for your expertise, we offer genuine professional freedom to pursue your ideas in a results-oriented environment. We offer a flexible working environment that gives you the autonomy to organise your own schedule and maintain a sustainable work-life balance.




The Role

We're seeking a technically capable Mid-Level (or above) Python Data Analyst to help our consulting team report on client sales performance from a recently developed OLAP cube environment. You'll hold partial, shared responsibility for the end-to-end data lifecycle across the OLAP infrastructure and data engineering.




Day to day, the core of the role will involve working with our client-facing consulting team to design and deliver client data reports and dashboards, partner with a DevOps engineer to build and deploy robust ETL pipelines, and maintain the integrity of our analytical schemas. You'll also work closely with our backend engineering team to productionise data flows that give clients precise, actionable insights.




A critical part of this role is recognising that sensitive client data needs different security policies and lifecycles from our public proprietary data sets. You'll advocate for strong data governance and security protocols with the Engineering team who build the infrastructure.




The ideal candidate is a Python and SQL specialist, ideally with some understanding of data engineering, who enjoys delivering unique insights through ETL and cares deeply about data quality in a scaling SaaS environment. We anticipate that as the core tasks gradually become automated, you'll want to explore other high value technological solutions to stretch your skills and deliver increasing value.




What you'll do (core responsibilities)

BI dashboarding: build custom client sales and strategic dashboards in Metabase, Apache Superset or similar. You'll be glad to know we do not run Microsoft products.
Python and SQL delivery: manipulate data, automate workflows, and support backend data processing using Pandas, NumPy and similar libraries.
Design analytical schemas: create optimised data models (for example, star schemas) for customer-facing consulting and reporting.
Internal tooling: build and maintain automated tools that let the consulting team run self-serve, ad-hoc queries.
Data quality assurance: produce data quality reports that directly steer and improve schema design.
Consulting collaboration: allocate roughly 20 to 30 percent of your bandwidth to supporting the delivery of live consulting projects and client needs.




Where you can grow (stretch opportunities)

This is not a pure reporting or dash-boarding role. As your capacity allows, we'd love you to take on more. Being a high-growth startup, the role offers ample opportunity to grow and get involved across the business, limited only by your appetite and motivation.




Data architecture: contribute to design decisions on the product's data structure and flow, and help shape the wider OLTP core data estate.
Semantic layer and modelling: help manage the semantic layer and optimise dbt and Cube models so our analytical schemas stay performant and robust.
Consulting solutions: help shape unique consulting delivery proposals alongside the team.
Mentorship and training: help budding pythonista consulting analysts write modular, reusable Python.
AI and advanced data models: help design and deliver AI processing and new data models, including graph data models we plan to adopt for some data sets.




Skills and experience

Essential

Python and SQL: strong, proven proficiency for data manipulation, automation and backend data processing.
BI tooling: hands-on experience with Metabase, Apache Superset or a comparable non-Microsoft BI tool.
OLAP data modelling: knowledge and experience of OLAP-related schemas, such as star schemas.
Notebooks: strong experience using Jupyter or Colab for prototyping and sharing ideas.
Data quality mindset: a genuine care for data quality in a scaling SaaS environment.




Desirable

Data engineering: an understanding of ETL design and productionising data flows.
Postgres depth: experience with Postgres syntax and extensions such as geospatial, pgvector, postgis and tlsh_pg (Trend Micro Locality Sensitive Hash).
Semantic layer tooling: experience with dbt and Cube.
Knowledge graphs: understanding of data architectures that harness graph data models and datastores.
Healthcare domain: interest in or experience with healthcare CRM or sales execution data.




Salary between £40,000 - £60,000 depending on experience.

Title: Senior Data Analyst - Digital Legal Delivery
Place: City Of London, England, United Kingdom
Description:
The Role

The Senior Data Analyst plays a critical role in delivering high‑impact analytics solutions across the firm. Working closely with partners, associates, and senior business stakeholders, the role leads complex analytical engagements, translating business needs into actionable insight and championing best practice in data analytics.

The role operates with a high degree of autonomy, managing multiple concurrent initiatives, collaborating and sharing knowledge with (junior) team members, and contributing directly to the firm's reputation for high‑quality, insight‑driven decision‑making.

This is an opportunity to shape the future of analytics at the firm, working on strategic initiatives with senior stakeholders while helping to grow a market‑leading analytics capability.

Key Responsibilities:

Leadership & Delivery

Lead the end‑to‑end delivery of complex analytics initiatives, ensuring high standards of quality, insight, and impact.

Manage multiple priorities and workstreams simultaneously, delivering to agreed timelines and stakeholder expectations.

Identify opportunities to deliver additional value from data by leveraging existing and emerging technologies, driving adoption of new analytical capabilities across the firm.

Analytics & Technical Expertise

Set and oversee best practice for the design and delivery of reports, dashboards, and insight across operational, financial, and performance metrics.

Undertake hands‑on development of complex dashboards and analytical products, demonstrating best‑in‑class data storytelling and visual analytics.

Apply advanced analytical techniques using SQL, Python, and relevant analytics platforms to solve complex business problems.

Incorporate Generative AI and AI‑enabled tools into analytics solutions where appropriate, enhancing efficiency, insight, and automation.

Stakeholder Engagement

Build trusted relationships with senior stakeholders, partners, and leadership teams to understand business challenges and shape analytics roadmaps.

Translate complex analytical findings into clear, compelling narratives for technical and non‑technical audiences.

Support stakeholders in improving data literacy and confidence in using insights to inform decision‑making.

Governance, Quality & Standards

Develop, implement and adhere to enterprise analytics standards, data quality controls, review practices and governance frameworks to ensure accuracy, consistency, and clarity.

Own and continuously improve business‑as‑usual BI and analytics processes, including the definition and tracking of relevant KPIs.

Ensure analytical outputs align with wider firm standards, risk requirements, and delivery frameworks.

Team Development

Contribute to team capability building through knowledge sharing and peer support on advanced analytical tasks.

Promote consistency in analytics practices across the firm, contributing to a cohesive and high‑quality approach to data and insights.

Qualifications, skills and experience

Essential

4+ years' experience in data or business analytics (professional services or law firm experience preferred).

Bachelor's degree in a STEM-related discipline (or equivalent experience).

Advanced skills in data visualisation and dashboarding, with hands-on experience in Power BI or similar tools (e.g. Tableau, QlikView).

Practical experience using Large Language Models (LLMs) and AI‑powered tools (e.g. Microsoft Copilot Studio or similar AI assistant platforms) to enhance analytics, automate workflows, or generate insights.

Strong proficiency in SQL and Python or equivalent programming language for data analysis, transformation, and automation. Working knowledge of SharePoint, Power Automate, Microsoft Fabric, or comparable platforms.

Excellent communication skills, with the ability to engage effectively with both technical and non‑technical stakeholders.

Strong analytical, problem‑solving, and critical‑thinking capability.

Proven ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver to tight deadlines in an Agile environment.

High attention to detail, with strong documentation and collaboration skills.

Demonstrated experience contributing as a (senior) member of an analytics or data team, with the ability to take ownership of complex analytical work.

Desirable

Experience working in a global or distributed team environment.

Demonstrated ability to drive continuous improvement and embed sustainable process change.

Agile or delivery‑management qualifications.

Experience coaching or line‑managing junior analysts, including identifying development needs.

Ability to translate business and user requirements into technical integration specifications. Experience with APIs (including REST services) and AI integration protocols such as MCP (Model Context Protocol).

Closing date for applications will be Friday 21 August at 12 pm.

Must be UK-based; must not live in Northern Ireland and must live at least 100 miles away from a HSF Kramer London office, otherwise location agnostic

Title: Data Analyst - Fraud
Description:
Who We Are

Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month.

As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually.

Curious about what makes Moniepoint an incredible place to work? Check out posts on how we cultivate a culture of innovation, teamwork, and growth.

What You Will Get To Do


Investigate fraud attacks, quantify their impact, and present clear findings that drive prioritisation and response
Propose and refine rule-based mitigations, working with fraud operations and engineering to see them through to implementation
Build and maintain reporting and dashboards to monitor fraud trends, rule performance, and key operational metrics
Work closely with fraud operations, data scientists, engineers, and product managers to ensure analytical insights translate into action
Proactively identify emerging patterns and flag risks before they escalate


To succeed in this role, you should have


Proven experience as a Data Analyst (Fraud), or a similar role (4+ years, can be made up for with accomplishments)
Strong problem solving skills
Advanced proficiency with SQL. you're comfortable writing complex queries to investigate and slice data across large datasets
Experience in fraud, risk, or financial services; you understand how fraud attacks work and how to think about mitigation trade-offs
A proactive mindset — you don't wait to be asked; you spot something unusual and you dig in
Some exposure to Python or scripting for data manipulation and analysis
Proficiency with a BI tool (PowerBI, Looker, Tableau, Superset, Redash, or any other alternative)
Strong stakeholder management skills; you can communicate findings clearly to fraud operations, product managers, engineers, and senior leadership — and you know how to influence decisions with data across all of them.
Comfort working in fast-paced, cross-functional teams where priorities shift quickly.
Proficiency with a spreadsheet tool (Microsoft Excel or Google Sheets, or any other alternative)
Enjoy autonomy and a flat structure: we have millions of customers and a flat hierarchy so any individual can have an outsized impact
Excellent written and verbal communication skills
A drive to learn and master new technologies and techniques
A bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Engineering, or any other related field


Experience With The Following Would Be a Plus


Data governance
Python or any other scripting language
Git or any other version control tool


What We Can Offer You


Culture - We put our people first and prioritise the well-being of every team member. We have built a company where all opinions carry weight and where all voices are heard. We value and respect each other and always look out for one another. Above all, we are human.
Learning - We have a learning and development-focused environment with an emphasis on knowledge sharing, training, and regular internal technical talks.
Compensation - You’ll receive an attractive salary, pension, health insurance, annual bonus, plus other benefits.


What To Expect In The Hiring Process


A preliminary phone call with the recruiter.
Technical take-home task (SQL test).
Technical Interview with hiring manager.
A behavioural interview with the Head of Data Analytics/Science and Fraud Team.


Moniepoint is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and candidates.

Title: Senior Data Analyst - Digital Legal Delivery
Description:
The Role

The Senior Data Analyst plays a critical role in delivering high‑impact analytics solutions across the firm. Working closely with partners, associates, and senior business stakeholders, the role leads complex analytical engagements, translating business needs into actionable insight and championing best practice in data analytics.

The role operates with a high degree of autonomy, managing multiple concurrent initiatives, collaborating and sharing knowledge with (junior) team members, and contributing directly to the firm's reputation for high‑quality, insight‑driven decision‑making.

This is an opportunity to shape the future of analytics at the firm, working on strategic initiatives with senior stakeholders while helping to grow a market‑leading analytics capability.

Key Responsibilities:

Leadership & Delivery

Lead the end‑to‑end delivery of complex analytics initiatives, ensuring high standards of quality, insight, and impact.

Manage multiple priorities and workstreams simultaneously, delivering to agreed timelines and stakeholder expectations.

Identify opportunities to deliver additional value from data by leveraging existing and emerging technologies, driving adoption of new analytical capabilities across the firm.

Analytics & Technical Expertise

Set and oversee best practice for the design and delivery of reports, dashboards, and insight across operational, financial, and performance metrics.

Undertake hands‑on development of complex dashboards and analytical products, demonstrating best‑in‑class data storytelling and visual analytics.

Apply advanced analytical techniques using SQL, Python, and relevant analytics platforms to solve complex business problems.

Incorporate Generative AI and AI‑enabled tools into analytics solutions where appropriate, enhancing efficiency, insight, and automation.

Stakeholder Engagement

Build trusted relationships with senior stakeholders, partners, and leadership teams to understand business challenges and shape analytics roadmaps.

Translate complex analytical findings into clear, compelling narratives for technical and non‑technical audiences.

Support stakeholders in improving data literacy and confidence in using insights to inform decision‑making.

Governance, Quality & Standards

Develop, implement and adhere to enterprise analytics standards, data quality controls, review practices and governance frameworks to ensure accuracy, consistency, and clarity.

Own and continuously improve business‑as‑usual BI and analytics processes, including the definition and tracking of relevant KPIs.

Ensure analytical outputs align with wider firm standards, risk requirements, and delivery frameworks.

Team Development

Contribute to team capability building through knowledge sharing and peer support on advanced analytical tasks.

Promote consistency in analytics practices across the firm, contributing to a cohesive and high‑quality approach to data and insights.

Qualifications, skills and experience

Essential

4+ years' experience in data or business analytics (professional services or law firm experience preferred).

Bachelor's degree in a STEM-related discipline (or equivalent experience).

Advanced skills in data visualisation and dashboarding, with hands-on experience in Power BI or similar tools (e.g. Tableau, QlikView).

Practical experience using Large Language Models (LLMs) and AI‑powered tools (e.g. Microsoft Copilot Studio or similar AI assistant platforms) to enhance analytics, automate workflows, or generate insights.

Strong proficiency in SQL and Python or equivalent programming language for data analysis, transformation, and automation. Working knowledge of SharePoint, Power Automate, Microsoft Fabric, or comparable platforms.

Excellent communication skills, with the ability to engage effectively with both technical and non‑technical stakeholders.

Strong analytical, problem‑solving, and critical‑thinking capability.

Proven ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver to tight deadlines in an Agile environment.

High attention to detail, with strong documentation and collaboration skills.

Demonstrated experience contributing as a (senior) member of an analytics or data team, with the ability to take ownership of complex analytical work.

Desirable

Experience working in a global or distributed team environment.

Demonstrated ability to drive continuous improvement and embed sustainable process change.

Agile or delivery‑management qualifications.

Experience coaching or line‑managing junior analysts, including identifying development needs.

Ability to translate business and user requirements into technical integration specifications. Experience with APIs (including REST services) and AI integration protocols such as MCP (Model Context Protocol).

Closing date for applications will be Friday 21 August at 12 pm.

Must be UK-based; must not live in Northern Ireland and must live at least 100 miles away from a HSF Kramer London office, otherwise location agnostic

Description:
Music is Universal

It’s the passionate and dedicated team at Universal Music who help make us the world’s leading music company. From A&R to finance, legal to digital, sales to marketing, Universal Music is the place to grow and develop your career within a truly commercial and innovative business that leads in everything it does.

Everyone is welcome to apply for our roles, and we are determined to ensure that no applicant or employee receives less favourable treatment because of gender, race, disability, sexual orientation, religion, belief, age, marital status, background, pregnancy, or caring responsibilities. We also recognise the importance of diversity of thought within our teams and are fully committed to embracing the talents of people with autism, dyslexia, ADHD, and other forms of neurocognitive variation.

We will always seek to make appropriate adjustments to recruitment, workplaces, and work processes to be fully inclusive to people with different needs and working styles. If you need us to make any reasonable adjustments for you from application onwards, including alternatives to the online form or to disclose a neurocognitive condition, please email UniversalMusicCareers@umusic.com.

Are you interested in working for the music industry? Would you like to help turn data into insight that drives innovation and creative data-driven strategies across Universal Music?

Universal Music UK is looking for a Senior Data Analyst to become part of our UK central data, AI and technology team. The role offers a unique opportunity to join us at the start of a new chapter, where we are looking to grow & expand on the foundation of work we’ve already begun.

The role is perfect for a candidate that is passionate about music, data, AI and technology and has a thirst for acquiring, analysing and communicating knowledge through data. In a creative organisation such as ours, reducing a complex problem into something simple is key, so any experience managing stakeholders, shaping questions and translating data into clear insight would also be a strength.

Alongside this, you will be responsible for delivering analysis, reporting and measurement that helps solve real business problems across Universal Music UK. You will work with stakeholders to understand business needs, define the right questions and turn complex data into clear, actionable insight. Working closely with data scientists, engineers, product managers and business teams, you will help improve how we measure performance, understand audiences and identify opportunities for our artists, labels and central teams. As we’re first and foremost a data, AI and technology team, you should be comfortable working with large datasets, technical teams and modern analytics tools.

As part of the central data, AI and technology team, you’ll have a chance to work across all divisions, including AMS, frontline labels, our catalogue division UMR, and all other central teams, as well as data and technology teams within the wider business. This includes helping shape insight, reporting and data products that support & supercharge the labels.

Key Responsibilities

Core responsibilities include:


Working directly with the Data & AI team to support artists & labels across the business.
Being a senior voice within the team and leading data strategy at a label level.
Supporting core strategic research with data & audience insight.
Researching & developing data driven solutions to solve current & future business problems.
Utilising partner data to pull out key metrics and feeding back to the label teams.
Advising on data related topics to help guide or inform business decisions.
Sourcing, cleaning and preparing data for modelling, product creation or visualisation.
Developing new data sets or features that become integral to how the business operates.


At the heart of this role is a desire to give us a competitive edge in connecting our artists with audiences across the globe. More will be explained at Interview. Rest assured, this is an exciting role as part of an innovative new initiative within the organisation.

Skills

Skills & Experience


Strong ability to translate complex datasets into clear, actionable insight.
Creative and commercially minded approach to problem-solving.
Strong stakeholder engagement, management and communication skills.
Ability to lead analytical projects from idea through to delivery and adoption.
Advanced SQL skills with experience querying large datasets accurately and efficiently.
Experience with cloud data platforms such as BigQuery, Google Cloud Platform or AWS.
Experience building dashboards, reporting products and self-serve insight tools.
Strong understanding of data modelling, ETL/ELT processes and data quality.
Working knowledge of Python or another programming language for analysis.
Familiarity with Git, version control and modern analytics workflows.
Good understanding of AI, machine learning concepts and their practical application.
Ability to mentor others and raise the quality of analytical work across a team.
Knowledge of music repertoire is advantageous.


Experience


Minimum of 4 years’ experience in a data analyst, analytics or related role.
Background engaging stakeholders in a consultative or analytical capacity.
Experience leading analysis that informs business decisions and product development.
Experience working with engineering, data science or product teams to turn analysis into scalable tools, reporting or data products.


Education


Degree in a relevant field or equivalent practical experience.
A background in Mathematics, Statistics, Computer Science, Physics, Economics, Data Science or a similarly analytical discipline would be advantageous.


Just So You Know…

However, the business operates in an environment that demands change and the jobholder's specific responsibilities and activities will vary and develop. Therefore, the job description should be seen as indicative and not as a permanent, definitive, and exhaustive statement.

Description:
Title: Data Analyst

Location: Bristol (Hybrid, 2-3 days per week in the office)

Salary: £50,000 - £60,000 DOE

Industry: SaaS




The Opportunity

I'm currently working with a fast-growing SaaS organisation based in Bristol that is looking to hire a Data Analyst to join its growing data and analytics function.




This is an excellent opportunity to play a key role in turning data into meaningful insights that support decision-making across the business. You'll work closely with stakeholders across commercial, product, marketing and operational teams to understand business requirements, analyse data and deliver reporting that helps drive performance.




The business is continuing to invest in its data capabilities, making this an exciting time to join a growing technology organisation where data is becoming increasingly central to how the business operates.




If you're passionate about using data to solve business problems, enjoy working closely with stakeholders and want to make a tangible impact within a SaaS environment, this could be an excellent next step in your career.




Key Responsibilities

Analyse business and customer data to identify trends, opportunities and areas for improvement.
Design, develop and maintain dashboards and reports for stakeholders across the organisation.
Gather reporting requirements from business users and translate them into effective analytical solutions.
Develop and maintain SQL queries to extract, manipulate and analyse data.
Produce regular KPI, performance and management reporting.
Work closely with commercial, product, marketing and operational teams to understand business challenges and provide data-driven recommendations.
Support ad-hoc analysis to answer key business questions and inform strategic decisions.
Ensure the accuracy, consistency and quality of reporting across multiple data sources.
Identify opportunities to improve reporting processes and data visibility across the business.
Communicate analytical findings clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Title: Data Insight Analyst
Description:
About MIB




At MIB our people are passionate about making roads safer by getting uninsured and hit-and-run drivers off our roads. Working in partnership with the Police, Insurers and Government our collective aim is to make it a thing of the past but, until that’s accomplished, we’re here to compensate victims quickly, fairly and compassionately.




Last year we helped more than 34,000 people struck by uninsured and hit-and-run drivers and paid over £400 million in compensation to support victims rebuild their lives.




About the role




The Data Insight Analyst will play a key role within the MIB Data Team, delivering high‑quality analysis and insight from complex datasets to support strategic and operational decision‑making.
The role will focus on in‑depth analytical work, translating data into clear, actionable insights, and working closely with business stakeholders and the Data Development team to ensure data solutions meet business needs.
The Data Insight Analyst working with the wider Data team, will act as a bridge between data and the business, combining strong technical capability with an understanding of business context to influence outcomes through evidence‑based insight.




Key responsibilities




Conduct in‑depth exploratory and statistical analysis on large and complex data sets to identify trends, patterns, risks, and opportunities.
Develop and test hypotheses based on a strong understanding of MIB data.
Combine MIB datasets with selected external data to broaden understanding and contextualise MIB data.
Develop clear, well‑structured analytical outputs that translate technical findings into meaningful business insight.
Apply analytical techniques to answer both ad‑hoc and recurring business questions.
Work closely with business partners & stakeholders to understand requirements, define analytical questions, and shape insight outputs.
Present findings and recommendations to both technical and non‑technical audiences in a clear and compelling way.
Act as a trusted analytical partner, supporting evidence‑based decision‑making across the organisation.
Collaborate with the Data Development team to shape data models, pipelines, and datasets that support analytical and reporting needs.
Validate data quality and ensure analytical outputs are robust, accurate, and fit for purpose.
Contribute to the continuous improvement of analytical tools, processes, and standards within the team.
Support the development and enhancement of insight‑led reporting and dashboards.
Ensure insights are aligned to organisational priorities and performance measures.
Document analytical approaches, assumptions, and methodologies to support transparency and reuse.




Skills and Experience




Strong experience working with large, complex datasets in a data analytics or insight role.
Advanced experience using Databricks, including working with Spark‑based data environments.
Strong Python skills, with hands‑on experience using Pandas and related analytical libraries.
Experience writing efficient, well‑structured code for data manipulation and analysis.
Good understanding of data warehousing concepts and analytical data models.
Experience working with cloud‑based data platforms (Azure preferred).
Strong analytical mindset with the ability to break down complex problems and apply structured thinking.
Ability to interpret data critically, challenge assumptions, and draw meaningful conclusions.
Ability to communicate complex analytical concepts clearly to non‑technical audiences.
Strong stakeholder management skills, with experience working across technical and business teams.
Confident presenting insights, recommendations, and options to support decision‑making.
Experience supporting reporting and insight functions in a regulated or complex environment.
Familiarity with data visualisation tools (e.g. Power BI, Databricks One or similar).
Experience working in Agile or sprint‑based delivery environments (e.g. Azure DevOps).
Curious and proactive, with a strong desire to understand the “why” behind the data.
Collaborative and team‑focused, with a willingness to share knowledge and best practice.
Organised and able to manage multiple priorities effectively.
Committed to continuous learning and development in data and analytics.

Title: Claims Data Analyst
Description:
About Zego



At Zego, we understand that traditional motor insurance holds good drivers back. It's too complicated, too expensive, and it doesn't reflect how well you actually drive. Since 2016, we have been on a mission to change that by offering the lowest priced insurance for good drivers.

From van drivers and gig workers to everyday car drivers, our customers are the driving force behind everything we do. We've sold tens of millions of policies and raised over $200 million in funding and picked up numerous awards, including the Insurance Claims Team Of The Year 2024 as awarded at The Insurance Post's Claims & Fraud Awards. And we're only just getting started.

Purpose of the role



We're looking for a proactive and analytical Claims Data Analyst to help us enhance our Claims and Fraud operations, shaping one of the most vital areas of the insurance industry.

As part of a fast-growing, product-led tech company, you'll play a key role in driving impactful change within our rapidly scaling Claims team. Your insights will power strategic decision-making, improve efficiency, and uncover opportunities for continuous improvement. Expect to work on developing insightful reports and dashboards, collaborating closely with Claims and Fraud teams, and delivering data-backed recommendations to leadership and stakeholders across the business.

If you thrive in a fast-paced, data-centric environment and are eager to make a real difference in the evolution of claims operations, we'd love to hear from you!

What you will be doing


Design & build core data models and reporting to support Claims and Fraud operations
Develop key reports for senior stakeholders, including Zego leadership, investors, and insurance partners
Analyze performance & identify trends, uncovering key drivers to optimise processes
Spot and size opportunities for continuous improvement, tracking the impact of initiatives
Support strategic decision-making for the Claims and Fraud leadership team
Translate data into compelling stories—delivering actionable insights to senior management
Collaborate cross-functionally, supporting Claims, Fraud, Pricing, and external reporting needs
What you will need to be successful


Got a degree? Great! If not, equivalent experience works too (bonus points if it's in a STEM subject)
SQL Skills - You know your way around data extraction and manipulation like a pro
Power BI Expertise - You've built data models, reports, and dashboards before and can turn raw numbers into something meaningful
Data Storytelling - You can take complex insights and turn them into clear, engaging stories that senior stakeholders (think senior managers, investors, Zego's board, and insurance partners) actually understand
Insurance Know-How (Nice to have!) - If you understand the motor insurance market and what drives commercial performance, that's a big plus
Claims & Financial Acumen (Nice to have!) - Familiarity with claims processes, reserving, and settlements? Even better
Actuarial & Reserving Knowledge (Nice to have!) - If you can be the go-to person between Claims, Fraud, and Actuarial teams, we'd love to have you on board!
What's it like to work at Zego?



Joining Zego is a career-defining move. People go further here, reaching their full potential to achieve extraordinary things. 

We're spread throughout the UK and Europe, and united by our drive to get things done. We're proud of our company and our culture - a friendly and inclusive space where we can lift each other up and celebrate our wins every day.

Together, we're setting the bar higher, delivering exceptional work that makes a difference. Our people are the most important part of our story, and everyone here plays a role. There's loads of room to learn and grow, and you'll get the freedom to steer your career wherever you want.

You'll work alongside a talented group who embrace each other's differences and aren't afraid of a challenge. We recognise our achievements, learn from our mistakes, and help each other to be the best we can be. Together, we're making insurance matter.
